+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Extraction.CharacterConsistency
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Extraction.EncodingSupport
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Extraction.Observables
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Extraction.PolynomialCollision
+
+/-!
+# Polynomial outcomes in the pulling argument
+
+The joint measurement of a polynomial marginal and an ideal Pauli register
+returns the difference between the polynomial and the encoding of the register.
+Decoding this difference gives exactly the pulled-apart measurement. Polynomial
+collision estimates apply to these representatives without an encoding-support
+restriction on the original marginal.
+
+## References
+
+- Blueprint `lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`, Item 2.
+- `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1530-1605`,
+  `eq:qld-pulling-11`, `eq:qld-pulling-12`, and the following symmetry argument.
+- `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex`; only decoder linearity and its
+  left-inverse identity are used here.
+- Issue #520; these auxiliary results do not assert `eq:qld-pulling-cons`.
+- The collision estimate compares unequal difference polynomials under uniform
+  evaluation.
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
+open MIPStarRE.Quantum DistanceCalculus
+open WinImplications
+
+noncomputable section
+
+open scoped Classical
+
+/-- The outcome `g - g_h` in `eq:qld-pulling-12` is a bounded polynomial
+representative, even when `g` is not in the encoding image. -/
+def pullingPoly {P : AdmissibleParams} (outcome : Poly P × PauliRegister P) : Poly P :=
+  outcome.1 - encodingPoly outcome.2
+
+/-- Decoder linearity identifies the label in `eq:qld-pulling-12`. This uses
+`Dec(g_h) = h`, never the reverse identity on arbitrary polynomials. -/
+theorem decodeFq_pullingPoly {P : AdmissibleParams}
+    (outcome : Poly P × PauliRegister P) :
+    decodeFq (pullingPoly outcome) = decodeFq outcome.1 - outcome.2 := by
+  have hsub (g h : Poly P) : decodeFq (g - h) = decodeFq g - decodeFq h := by
+    funext y
+    simp [decodeOn, decodeAt, evalPoly, MvPolynomial.eval_sub]
+  rw [pullingPoly, hsub, decodeFq_lowDegreeEncoding]
+
+/-- Equal difference polynomials give identical scalar labels in the symmetric
+expression following `eq:qld-pulling-12`, for every register vector. -/
+theorem pulling_label_eq_of_poly_eq {P : AdmissibleParams}
+    (first second : Poly P × PauliRegister P)
+    (h : pullingPoly first = pullingPoly second) (u : PauliRegister P) :
+    dotProduct (decodeFq first.1 - first.2) u =
+      dotProduct (decodeFq second.1 - second.2) u := by
+  rw [← decodeFq_pullingPoly, ← decodeFq_pullingPoly, h]
+
+/-- The projective measurement with polynomial outcomes `g - g_h` used to
+organize the last step of the pulling argument. Its input witness remains
+supplied; no global witness is constructed by this definition. -/
+def pullingMeas {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaG : ℝ}
+    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) :
+    Measurement (Poly P) (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace side)) :=
+  (tensorMeasurement (w.marginalPoly side W) (pauliRegisterMeas W)).postprocess pullingPoly
+
+/-- The joint effects are tensor products of orthogonal projections, and
+postprocessing retains projectivity. -/
+theorem pullingMeas_isProjective {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaG : ℝ}
+    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) :
+    Measurement.IsProjective (pullingMeas w side W) := by
+  apply SandwichProduct.postprocess_isProjective
+  intro outcome
+  exact MakingMeasurementsProjective.isProj_kronecker
+    (w.marginalPoly_isProjective side W outcome.1)
+    ⟨by simp [IsIdempotentElem, pauliRegisterMeas, Measurement.ofSumEqOne,
+        pauliProj_mul_pauliProj],
+      (posSemidef_pauliProj W outcome.2).isHermitian⟩
+
+/-- Decoding the difference-polynomial measurement recovers `eq:tilde_M`
+exactly. The equality holds on the full bounded polynomial carrier. -/
+theorem pullingMeas_postprocess_effect {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaG : ℝ}
+    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) :
+    ((pullingMeas w side W).postprocess (fun g => dotProduct (decodeFq g) u)).effect a =
+      tildeM w side W u a := by
+  classical
+  rw [pullingMeas, Measurement.postprocess_comp]
+  simp only [Measurement.postprocess_effect, Finset.sum_filter,
+    decodeFq_pullingPoly, tensorMeasurement, Measurement.ofSumEqOne, pauliRegisterMeas]
+  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
+  unfold tildeM tauDotProj bracketOp
+  simp_rw [heteroKron_finset_sum_right, Finset.sum_filter]
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro g _
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro h _
+  have hlabel : dotProduct (decodeFq g - h) u = a ↔
+      dotProduct h u = dotProduct (decodeFq g) u - a := by
+    rw [sub_dotProduct]
+    constructor <;> intro heq <;> linear_combination -heq
+  simp only [hlabel]
+
+/-- The coordinate change to two extraction blocks preserves the consistency
+defect, including every off-diagonal outcome and the question distribution. -/
+private theorem consistencyDefect_placeSide_eq {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon : ℝ}
+    {X A : Type*} [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype A] [DecidableEq A]
+    (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon) (mu : Distribution X)
+    (left : X → A → Op (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace .alice)))
+    (right : X → A → Op (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace .bob))) :
+    consistencyDefect mu (fun x a => S.placeSide .alice (left x a))
+        (fun x a => S.placeSide .bob (right x a)) S.psiHat =
+      consistencyDefect mu (fun x a => heteroKron (left x a) 1)
+        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 (right x a))
+        (reindexState (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) S.psiHat) := by
+  unfold consistencyDefect
+  apply avgOver_congr
+  intro x
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro a _
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro b _
+  by_cases hab : a = b
+  · simp only [hab, if_true]
+  · simp only [if_neg hab, consistency_term_eq_stateQForm]
+    rw [stateQForm_reindexState, reindexOp_mul]
+    rfl
+
+/-- Polynomial collision and deterministic decoding, before choosing a
+register placement. This separates the finite probability calculation from
+the six-register coordinate identities. -/
+private theorem polynomial_decoding_defect_le_evaluated_add {P : AdmissibleParams}
+    {I J : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
+    (A : Measurement (Poly P) I) (B : Measurement (Poly P) J)
+    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J)) (hpsi : ‖psi‖ = 1) :
+    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (PauliRegister P))
+        (fun u a => heteroKron
+          ((A.postprocess (fun g => dotProduct (decodeFq g) u)).effect a) 1)
+        (fun u a => heteroKron 1
+          ((B.postprocess (fun g => dotProduct (decodeFq g) u)).effect a)) psi ≤
+      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
+        (fun u a => heteroKron ((A.postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a) 1)
+        (fun u a => heteroKron 1 ((B.postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a)) psi +
+          (P.m * P.d : ℝ) / P.q := by
+  have hcollision := SandwichProduct.point_codeword_defect_le_avg_evaluated_add
+    A B psi evalPoly ((P.m * P.d : ℝ) / P.q) hpsi
+    (by positivity) (fun g h hne => poly_eval_collision_le g h hne)
+  have hpost (u : PauliRegister P) := consistencyDefect_postprocess_le
+    (uniformDistribution Unit) (fun _ => A) (fun _ => B) psi
+    (fun g => dotProduct (decodeFq g) u)
+  simp only [consistencyDefect, avgOver_uniform_const,
+    consistency_term_eq_stateQForm, placed_product_stateQForm_eq] at hpost
+  simp only [consistencyDefect, consistency_term_eq_stateQForm,
+    placed_product_stateQForm_eq]
+  exact (avgOver_mono _ _ _ hpost).trans
+    ((avgOver_uniform_const _).le.trans hcollision)
+
+/-- The last polynomial-collision step of the pulling argument, followed by
+decoding. The field-measurement defect is bounded by the evaluated
+difference-polynomial defect plus exactly `m * d / q`.
+
+This is an unconditional comparison of two actual defects for the supplied
+measurement. Bounding the evaluated defect from the witness's point
+consistency remains the preceding steps of `eq:qld-pulling-cons`; no estimate
+for that defect is assumed here. The state and placements are the original
+six-register ones. -/
+theorem tildeM_consistencyDefect_le_pulling_eval_add {P : AdmissibleParams}
+    {epsilon deltaG : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon}
+    (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG) (W : PauliKind) :
+    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (PauliRegister P))
+        (fun u a => S.placeSide .alice (tildeM w .alice W u a))
+        (fun u a => S.placeSide .bob (tildeM w .bob W u a)) S.psiHat ≤
+      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
+        (fun u a => S.placeSide .alice
+          (((pullingMeas w .alice W).postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a))
+        (fun u a => S.placeSide .bob
+          (((pullingMeas w .bob W).postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a))
+        S.psiHat + (P.m * P.d : ℝ) / P.q := by
+  classical
+  rw [consistencyDefect_placeSide_eq, consistencyDefect_placeSide_eq]
+  have h := polynomial_decoding_defect_le_evaluated_add
+      (pullingMeas w .alice W) (pullingMeas w .bob W)
+      (reindexState (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) S.psiHat)
+      (by rw [reindexState_norm_eq, S.psiHat_norm])
+  simp only [pullingMeas_postprocess_effect] at h
+  convert h using 1
+  all_goals congr 1
+
+/-- Observable consistency reduces to the evaluated difference-polynomial
+defect. The coefficient four, uniform register average, and fixed basis
+coordinate are exactly those of the established character conversion.
+This estimate assumes no bound on the remaining evaluated defect. -/
+theorem tildeObs_opDistSq_le_pulling_eval_add {P : AdmissibleParams}
+    {epsilon deltaG : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon}
+    (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG) (W : PauliKind) (j : Fin P.model.basisDim) :
+    opDistSq (uniformDistribution (PauliRegister P))
+        (fun u => S.placeSide .alice (tildeObs w .alice W u j))
+        (fun u => S.placeSide .bob (tildeObs w .bob W u j)) S.psiHat ≤
+      4 * (consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
+        (fun u a => S.placeSide .alice
+          (((pullingMeas w .alice W).postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a))
+        (fun u a => S.placeSide .bob
+          (((pullingMeas w .bob W).postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a))
+        S.psiHat + (P.m * P.d : ℝ) / P.q) := by
+  exact (tildeObs_opDistSq_le_four_consistencyDefect w W j).trans
+    (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (tildeM_consistencyDefect_le_pulling_eval_add w W)
+      (by norm_num))
+
+end
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    80	    him, mul_zero, sub_zero]

    82	end Factorization

    84	/-- An additive convolution of effect families can be indexed by the ancillary
    85	answer alone. This is the finite-fiber form of the expanded point construction. -/
    86	theorem sum_add_fiber_heteroKron {G ι κ : Type*}
    87	    [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G] [AddCommGroup G]
    88	    (A : G → Op ι) (R : G → Op κ) (z : G) :
    89	    (∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p : G × G => p.1 + p.2 = z),
    90	      heteroKron (A p.1) (R p.2)) =
    91	      ∑ c : G, heteroKron (A (z - c)) (R c) := by
    92	  rw [Finset.sum_filter, Fintype.sum_prod_type, Finset.sum_comm]
    93	  simp only [← eq_sub_iff_add_eq, Finset.sum_ite_eq', Finset.mem_univ, if_true]
    94	
    95	/-- Averaging a common additive shift preserves the off-diagonal mass of any
    96	weight function. The ancillary joint weights are supported on the diagonal
    97	and have total diagonal mass one. -/
    98	private theorem sum_convolution_off_diagonal_eq {G : Type*}
    99	    [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G] [AddCommGroup G]
   100	    (p q : G → G → ℝ) (hzero : ∀ c d, c ≠ d → q c d = 0)
   101	    (hdiag : ∑ c : G, q c c = 1) :
   102	    (∑ z : G, ∑ w : G, if z = w then 0 else
   103	      ∑ c : G, ∑ d : G, p (z - c) (w - d) * q c d) =
   104	      ∑ a : G, ∑ b : G, if a = b then 0 else p a b := by
   105	  have hinner (z w c : G) :
   106	      (∑ d : G, p (z - c) (w - d) * q c d) =
   107	        p (z - c) (w - c) * q c c := by
   108	    apply Finset.sum_eq_single c
   109	    · intro d _ hdc
   110	      rw [hzero c d hdc.symm, mul_zero]
   111	    · simp
   112	  have hshift (c : G) :
   113	      (∑ z : G, ∑ w : G, if z = w then 0 else p (z - c) (w - c)) =
   114	        ∑ a : G, ∑ b : G, if a = b then 0 else p a b := by
   115	    refine Fintype.sum_equiv (Equiv.subRight c) _ _ fun z => ?_
   116	    refine Fintype.sum_equiv (Equiv.subRight c) _ _ fun w => ?_
   117	    change (if z = w then 0 else p (z - c) (w - c)) =
   118	      if z - c = w - c then 0 else p (z - c) (w - c)
   119	    simp only [sub_left_inj]
   120	  simp_rw [hinner]
   121	  calc
   122	    (∑ z : G, ∑ w : G, if z = w then 0 else
   123	        ∑ c : G, p (z - c) (w - c) * q c c) =
   124	        ∑ z : G, ∑ w : G, ∑ c : G,
   125	          (if z = w then 0 else p (z - c) (w - c)) * q c c := by
   126	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   127	      intro z _
   128	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   129	      intro w _
   130	      by_cases hzw : z = w <;> simp [hzw]
   131	    _ = ∑ c : G, (∑ z : G, ∑ w : G,
   132	        if z = w then 0 else p (z - c) (w - c)) * q c c := by
   133	      simp_rw [Finset.sum_mul]
   134	      conv_lhs =>
   135	        arg 2
   136	        ext z
   137	        rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   138	      rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   139	    _ = _ := by
   140	      simp_rw [hshift]
   141	      rw [← Finset.mul_sum, hdiag, mul_one]
   142	
   143	/-- Independent additive convolution with a normalized, perfectly correlated
   144	ancillary POVM pair preserves the consistency defect exactly. All four register
   145	types may differ, and neither the original state nor the question distribution
   146	needs to be normalized. No measurement is assumed projective.
   147	
   148	This is a generic auxiliary for the expanded point construction in paper
   149	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-438` and
   150	`lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`, not the latter paper theorem. Its ancillary
   151	perfection hypothesis must be established for the concrete ideal measurements
   152	before specialization; that application is tracked in issue #267. -/
   153	theorem consistencyDefect_convolution_eq_of_perfect
   154	    {X G ιA ιB κA κB : Type*}
   155	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G] [AddCommGroup G]
   156	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   157	    [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA] [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB]
   158	    (μ : Distribution X) (A : X → Measurement G ιA) (B : X → Measurement G ιB)
   159	    (R : X → Measurement G κA) (T : X → Measurement G κB)
   160	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (κA × κB))
   161	    (hφ : ‖φ‖ = 1)
   162	    (hperfect : ∀ x, (∑ c : G, ∑ d : G, if c = d then 0 else
   163	      stateQForm φ (heteroKron ((R x).effect c) ((T x).effect d))) = 0) :
   164	    consistencyDefect μ
   165	        (fun x z => heteroKron
   166	          (∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p : G × G => p.1 + p.2 = z),
   167	            heteroKron ((A x).effect p.1) ((R x).effect p.2)) 1)
   168	        (fun x z => heteroKron 1
   169	          (∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p : G × G => p.1 + p.2 = z),
   170	            heteroKron ((B x).effect p.1) ((T x).effect p.2)))
   171	        (reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor ψ φ)) =
   172	      consistencyDefect μ (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).effect a) 1)
   173	        (fun x b => heteroKron 1 ((B x).effect b)) ψ := by
   174	  unfold consistencyDefect
   175	  simp_rw [consistency_term_eq_stateQForm, placed_product_stateQForm_eq]
   176	  apply avgOver_congr
   177	  intro x
   178	  let q : G → G → ℝ := fun c d =>
   179	    stateQForm φ (heteroKron ((R x).effect c) ((T x).effect d))
   180	  have hnonneg (c d : G) : 0 ≤ q c d :=
   181	    stateQForm_nonneg φ (kronecker_nonneg ((R x).pos c) ((T x).pos d))
   182	  have hoff (c d : G) : 0 ≤ (if c = d then 0 else q c d) := by
   183	    split_ifs
   184	    · exact le_rfl
   185	    · exact hnonneg c d
   186	  have hzero (c d : G) (hcd : c ≠ d) : q c d = 0 := by
   187	    have hrow := (Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg
   188	      (fun c _ => Finset.sum_nonneg (fun d _ => hoff c d))).mp (hperfect x)
   189	    have hterm := (Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg
   190	      (fun d _ => hoff c d)).mp (hrow c (Finset.mem_univ c)) d (Finset.mem_univ d)
   191	    simpa only [if_neg hcd] using hterm
   192	  have hdiag : ∑ c : G, q c c = 1 := by
   193	    have h := point_defect_eq (leftPlacedMeasurement (R x))
   194	      (rightPlacedMeasurement (T x)) φ
   195	    simp only [leftPlacedMeasurement, rightPlacedMeasurement, Measurement.ofSumEqOne,
   196	      placed_product_stateQForm_eq, hperfect x, hφ, one_pow] at h
   197	    dsimp only [q]
   198	    linarith
   199	  have hfactor (a b c d : G) := stateQForm_prodShuffle_vecTensor_heteroKron ψ φ
   200	    ((A x).effect a) ((B x).effect b) ((R x).pos c) ((T x).pos d)
   201	  simp_rw [sum_add_fiber_heteroKron, heteroKron_finset_sum_left,
   202	    heteroKron_finset_sum_right, stateQForm_finset_sum, hfactor]
   203	  exact sum_convolution_off_diagonal_eq
   204	    (fun a b => stateQForm ψ (heteroKron ((A x).effect a) ((B x).effect b)))
   205	    q hzero hdiag
   206	
   207	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    33	/-- Placing a tensor with an identity on Bob's last register recovers `BB'`. -/

    42	/-- The point factor on `A` and the factors on `BB'B''` can be regrouped as

    44	theorem placePlayer_alice_mul_placeSide_bob_tensor (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon)

    56	/-- Bob's extraction-block placement preserves finite sums. -/
    57	theorem placeSide_bob_finset_sum (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon)
    58	    {I : Type*} (s : Finset I) (B : I → Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιB)) :
    59	    S.placeSide .bob (∑ i ∈ s, B i) = ∑ i ∈ s, S.placeSide .bob (B i) := by
    60	  classical
    61	  change reindexOp (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
    62	    (heteroKron (1 : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιA)) (∑ i ∈ s, B i)) = _

    68	/-- The convolution formula with its second outcome solved for. This is the
    69	third line of the overlap calculation in paper lines 1483--1492. -/
    70	theorem pointMeasExp_effect_eq_sum_sub (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon)
    71	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
    72	    (a : PauliScalar P) :
    73	    (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a =
    74	      ∑ b : PauliScalar P, heteroKron ((S.pointMeas side W u).effect b)
    75	        (tauDotProj W (indicatorVec u) (a - b)) := by
    76	  classical
    77	  change S.expPointOp side W u a = _
    78	  rw [S.expPointOp_eq_convolution]

    80	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    81	  intro b _
    82	  have h (c : PauliScalar P) : b + c = a ↔ c = a - b := by
    83	    rw [eq_sub_iff_add_eq, add_comm]

    89	/-- The original/pulled-apart overlap is exactly the expanded-point overlap
    90	at the decoded value. This is the first three lines of the proof of Item 1 in
    91	paper lines 1483--1492; it holds for every polynomial outcome. -/
    92	theorem sum_pointMeas_mul_tildeM_eq_decoded_overlap
    93	    {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaG : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon}
    94	    (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG) (W : PauliKind)
    95	    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
    96	    (∑ a : PauliScalar P, S.placePlayer .alice ((S.pointMeas .alice W u).effect a) *
    97	      S.placeSide .bob (tildeM w .bob W (indicatorVec u) a)) =
    98	      ∑ g : Poly P, S.place .BB' ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).effect g) *
    99	        S.place .AB'' ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).effect
   100	          (dotProduct (decodeFq g) (indicatorVec u))) := by
   101	  classical
   102	  simp only [tildeM, S.placeSide_bob_finset_sum, Finset.mul_sum]
   103	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   104	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   105	  intro g _
   106	  simp only [S.placePlayer_alice_mul_placeSide_bob_tensor]
   107	  rw [← Finset.mul_sum, ← S.place_finset_sum,
   108	    S.pointMeasExp_effect_eq_sum_sub .alice W u]
   109	  rfl

   111	/-- The pulled-apart consistency defect is one minus the decoded overlap.
   112	This combines completeness with the first three lines of the source's
   113	calculation, still without imposing an encoding restriction. -/
   114	theorem tildeM_consistencyDefect_eq_one_sub_decoded_overlap
   115	    {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaG : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon}
   116	    (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG) (W : PauliKind) :
   117	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
   118	      (fun u a => S.placePlayer .alice ((S.pointMeas .alice W u).effect a))
   119	      (fun u a => S.placeSide .bob (tildeM w .bob W (indicatorVec u) a)) S.psiHat =
   120	      1 - avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) (fun u =>
   121	        ∑ g : Poly P, stateQForm S.psiHat
   122	          (S.place .BB' ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).effect g) *
   123	            S.place .AB'' ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).effect
   124	              (dotProduct (decodeFq g) (indicatorVec u))))) := by
   125	  classical
   126	  let point := fun u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P =>
   127	    S.placedMeasurement .AA' (leftPlacedMeasurement (S.pointMeas .alice W u))
   128	  let pulled : (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) → Measurement (PauliScalar P)
   129	      (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := fun u =>
   130	    Measurement.ofSumEqOne
   131	      (fun a => S.placeSide .bob (tildeM w .bob W (indicatorVec u) a))
   132	      (fun a => by
   133	        apply ProjectiveSetting.reindexOp_nonneg
   134	        exact kronecker_nonneg Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg
   135	          (tildeM_isProj w .bob W (indicatorVec u) a).nonneg)
   136	      (by
   137	        rw [← S.placeSide_bob_finset_sum, sum_tildeM_eq_one]
   138	        change reindexOp (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
   139	          (heteroKron (1 : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιA))
   140	            (1 : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιB))) = 1
   141	        rw [heteroKron_one_one]
   142	        ext row col
   143	        simp [reindexOp, Matrix.one_apply])
   144	  have h := consistencyDefect_eq_one_sub_overlap
   145	    (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) point pulled S.psiHat
   146	    (uniformDistribution_isProbability _) S.psiHat_norm
   147	  change consistencyDefect _ _ _ S.psiHat = 1 - avgOver _ (fun u =>
   148	    ∑ a : PauliScalar P, stateQForm S.psiHat
   149	      (S.placePlayer .alice ((S.pointMeas .alice W u).effect a) *
   150	        S.placeSide .bob (tildeM w .bob W (indicatorVec u) a))) at h
   151	  refine h.trans ?_
   152	  congr 1
   153	  apply avgOver_congr
   154	  intro u
   155	  rw [← stateQForm_finset_sum, sum_pointMeas_mul_tildeM_eq_decoded_overlap,
   156	    stateQForm_finset_sum]
   157

   159	/-- Replacing polynomial evaluation by decoded evaluation loses at most the
   160	mass of the non-encoding outcomes. This is the support-restricted replacement
   161	for the fourth line of paper lines 1483--1492. No mass estimate is assumed. -/
   162	theorem marginal_eval_overlap_le_decoded_add_nonencoding
   163	    {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaG : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon}
   164	    (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG) (W : PauliKind)
   165	    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   166	    (∑ g : Poly P, stateQForm S.psiHat
   167	      (S.place .BB' ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).effect g) *
   168	        S.place .AB'' ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).effect (MvPolynomial.eval u g.1)))) ≤
   169	      (∑ g : Poly P, stateQForm S.psiHat
   170	        (S.place .BB' ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).effect g) *
   171	          S.place .AB'' ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).effect
   172	            (dotProduct (decodeFq g) (indicatorVec u))))) +
   173	      ∑ g ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun g : Poly P => ¬ IsEncoding g),
   174	        stateQForm S.psiHat (S.place .BB' ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).effect g)) := by
   175	  classical
   176	  have hpos (g : Poly P) (a : PauliScalar P) :
   177	      0 ≤ stateQForm S.psiHat
   178	        (S.place .BB' ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).effect g) *
   179	          S.place .AB'' ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).effect a)) :=
   180	    stateQForm_nonneg _ (S.place_mul_place_nonneg .BB' .AB'' (by trivial)
   181	      ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).pos g) ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).pos a))
   182	  have hsum (g : Poly P) :
   183	      (∑ a : PauliScalar P, stateQForm S.psiHat
   184	        (S.place .BB' ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).effect g) *
   185	          S.place .AB'' ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).effect a))) =
   186	        stateQForm S.psiHat (S.place .BB' ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).effect g)) := by
   187	    have hc : (∑ a : PauliScalar P,
   188	        S.place .AB'' ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).effect a)) = 1 :=
   189	      (S.placedMeasurement .AB'' (S.pointMeasExp .alice W u)).sum_eq_one
   190	    rw [← stateQForm_finset_sum, ← Finset.mul_sum, hc, mul_one]
   191	  rw [Finset.sum_filter, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   192	  apply Finset.sum_le_sum
   193	  intro g _
   194	  by_cases hg : IsEncoding g
   195	  · simp only [hg, not_true_eq_false, if_false, add_zero]
   196	    rw [decodeFq_dotProduct_indicatorVec hg u]
   197	    rfl
   198	  · simp only [hg, not_false_eq_true, if_true]
   199	    have hle := Finset.single_le_sum (fun a _ => hpos g a)
   200	      (Finset.mem_univ (MvPolynomial.eval u g.1))
   201	    rw [hsum] at hle
   202	    exact hle.trans (le_add_of_nonneg_left (hpos g _))
   203	
   204	
   205	
   206	end

   137	/-- On Alice's marginal, replacing polynomial evaluation by decoded evaluation
   138	loses at most the non-encoding mass. This is the support-restricted version of
   139	the fourth line of paper lines 1483--1492, with the players interchanged. -/

   141	    {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaG : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon}
   142	    (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG) (W : PauliKind)
   143	    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :

   146	        S.place .BA'' ((S.pointMeasExp .bob W u).effect (MvPolynomial.eval u g.1)))) ≤
   147	      (∑ g : Poly P, stateQForm S.psiHat

   149	          S.place .BA'' ((S.pointMeasExp .bob W u).effect
   150	            (dotProduct (decodeFq g) (indicatorVec u))))) +
   151	      ∑ g ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun g : Poly P => ¬ IsEncoding g),
   152	        stateQForm S.psiHat (S.place .AA' ((w.marginalPoly .alice W).effect g)) := by
   153	  classical

   157	          S.place .BA'' ((S.pointMeasExp .bob W u).effect a)) :=
   158	    stateQForm_nonneg _ (S.place_mul_place_nonneg .AA' .BA'' (by trivial)
   159	      ((w.marginalPoly .alice W).pos g) ((S.pointMeasExp .bob W u).pos a))

   161	      (∑ a : PauliScalar P, stateQForm S.psiHat
   162	        (S.place .AA' ((w.marginalPoly .alice W).effect g) *
   163	          S.place .BA'' ((S.pointMeasExp .bob W u).effect a))) =
   164	        stateQForm S.psiHat (S.place .AA' ((w.marginalPoly .alice W).effect g)) := by

   166	        S.place .BA'' ((S.pointMeasExp .bob W u).effect a)) = 1 :=
   167	      (S.placedMeasurement .BA'' (S.pointMeasExp .bob W u)).sum_eq_one

   178	      (Finset.mem_univ (MvPolynomial.eval u g.1))

    81	    rfl
    82	  rw [← hmass_eq] at hcompare
    83	  rw [tildeM_consistencyDefect_eq_one_sub_decoded_overlap]

   215	\[
   216		B = \delta_G + \sqrt{\eps} + \frac{md}{q}.

    93	\section{The range-projection obligation}
    94	
    95	Lines~1827--1858 prove state-dependent closeness for the concrete operators
    96	obtained by conjugating the original measurement with the swap unitaries.
    97	Lines~1864--1875 then define isometries by adjoining EPR pairs and applying
    98	those unitaries, and immediately state the corresponding closeness for
    99	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger$.  The omitted range projection makes this implication
   100	non-definitional \cite[lines~1827--1875]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
   101	
   102	Let $\Psi$ be the original state and suppose $\phi\Psi$ is close to the ideal
   103	state $\Delta$.  Since $Q\phi\Psi=\phi\Psi$ and $Q$ is a contraction, the
   104	triangle inequality bounds $(I-Q)\Delta$ by the state-extraction error.  Using
   105	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ$, split
   106	\[
   107	  (N_hQ-T_h)\Delta
   108	  =(N_h-T_h)\Delta-N_h(I-Q)\Delta,
   109	\]
   110	where $T_h$ is the ideal Pauli projector.  Summing squared norms over $h$
   111	uses projectivity and orthogonality to keep the second term under control.
   112	The same argument is required for each player and each Pauli basis.
   113	
   114	This transfer is an open proof obligation for the next extraction stage.  It
   115	must be a theorem derived from the concrete swap unitaries, transformed-state
   116	estimate, and operator comparisons.  It must not be stored as a bridge field,
   117	residual assumption, or hypothesis of the source-labelled soundness theorem.

    17	\section{Purpose}
    18	
    19	When a formalization relies on a cited mathematical source, the cited source
    20	should remain intact.  It is a source, not an errata file.  If a possible gap,
    21	missing hypothesis, incorrect numerical constant, or other mathematical
    22	discrepancy is found, the matter should be recorded in a separate LaTeX note.
    23	In this repository such notes live under \path{docs/paper-gaps/}.  The same
    24	principle applies when the formal development has already diverged from the
    25	cited source, for instance by changing a statement so that it compiles, or by
    26	using a different mathematical route because an available formal-library theorem
    27	has a slightly different form.  Such a note is a mathematical note first, and a
    28	record of the formalization second: it should be readable by a mathematician or
    29	mathematical physicist who has not followed the issue discussion.
    30	
    31	The note should isolate the mathematical mechanism.  It should say what the
    32	cited source asserts, what the cited results actually imply, where a term or
    33	hypothesis is lost, and what statement the formal development proves instead.
    34	If the formal proof takes a different route, the note should explain the
    35	replacement argument and the hypotheses on which it rests.  This is especially
    36	important when the proof uses a theorem, construction, or convention from
    37	Mathlib which is not part of the cited argument.  In that case the note should
    38	state the Mathlib result in ordinary mathematical language, explain how it is
    39	specialized to the notation of the paper, and compare its hypotheses and
    40	conclusion with the step it replaces.  It should not merely say that \Lean{} did
    41	not accept a proof, that the modified proof compiles, or that a named library
    42	lemma was applied.
    43	
    44	The documents in this directory should themselves follow this standard.  A
    45	policy or template which reads like a checklist will tend to produce checklist
    46	notes; the examples and templates should therefore be written as mathematical
    47	prose.
    48	
    49	\section{Concision and Readability}
    50	
    51	A paper-gap note should be short enough that a reader can understand the issue
    52	in one sitting.  The first page should answer four questions: what the source
    53	uses, how hard the remaining formal work is, what the formalization or audit
    54	checked, and what the current verdict is.  Begin with a short
    55	\emph{At a glance} section when the note concerns an open or recently resolved
    56	formalization task.  That section should estimate the difficulty, the rough
    57	implementation weight, the split between Mathlib reuse and project-local work,
    58	and the key Mathlib APIs or modules.  Use honest ranges, not false precision.
    59	
    60	The \emph{Key theorem forms} section should be Section~2, immediately after
    61	\emph{At a glance}.  Put the theorem forms before the source details so the
    62	reader knows what the formalization is aiming to prove.  After that, keep the
    63	source assertion, the mechanism being checked, the blueprint/formal comparison,
    64	and the conclusion.  Use more sections only when a counterexample or long
    65	derivation genuinely needs room.
    66	
    67	Keep background to the minimum needed for the local point.  Prefer one clear
    68	special case over a general restatement of the surrounding theorem.  Use displayed
    69	equations for the source assertion, the key calculation, and the theorem forms;
    70	avoid displays for traceability data, declaration names, or long lists.  The
    71	blueprint/formal comparison should be compact and should not repeat the theorem
    72	forms.  The section ``Form of the Note'' below specifies where traceability data
    73	belongs; the body should read as mathematical prose, not as a log.
    74	
    75	If the verdict is that there is no mathematical discrepancy, say so plainly and
    76	stop.  Keep the conclusion highly compact, normally under twenty source lines.
    77	If the only remaining work is an implementation task, name it briefly and link
    78	the issue or pull request in a footnote.
    79	
    80	\section{When the Investigation Starts}
    81	
    82	The investigation starts when the obstruction appears to be mathematical rather
    83	than merely formal.  No final judgement is needed at this stage.  It is enough
    84	that, after reading the relevant source and attempting the corresponding formal
    85	statement, the proof seems to require a different scalar, an additional
    86	hypothesis, a different tensor placement, a distinction between two objects which
    87	the prose identifies, or an auxiliary assertion not supplied by the cited
    88	argument.
    89	
    90	The same investigation should also start when such a deviation is discovered
    91	after the fact.  If the existing formal development or informal blueprint has
    92	already changed the statement, strengthened a hypothesis, weakened a conclusion,
    93	inserted an unadvertised lemma, or replaced the cited proof by a different
    94	formal-library argument, the mathematical change should be documented even if all
    95	relevant files already compile.
    96	
    97	At this early stage the purpose is to preserve the question while it is still
    98	local.  The note may later conclude that the matter is only notational, that an
    99	intermediate estimate in the cited source needs a harmless correction, that a
   100	missing hypothesis is genuinely needed, or that no discrepancy remains.  Thus
   101	the trigger is not the severity of the eventual verdict, but the appearance of a
   102	real mismatch between the cited reasoning and the statement that can be
   103	formalized.
   104	
   105	A failed tactic search, a missing formal lemma, or an inconvenient coercion is
   106	not enough.  The obstruction must survive translation back into ordinary
   107	mathematics.
   108	
   109	Once a cited statement is established to be mathematically false, the repair
   110	and escalation procedure is governed by Section~6 of
   111	\path{local/protocols/issues-prs.md}.  Before asking the human owner to choose a
   112	replacement, a dedicated mathematical-gap session must produce a correction
   113	which is correct, sufficient for every paper and blueprint use, and minimal,
   114	then iterate it against the Lean statement and its downstream consumers.  A
   115	Claude Fable~5.1 session is currently launched by the owner session through its
   116	Agent tool; a Codex main session requests that lane on progress log~\#27 rather
   117	than dispatching a Codex worker.  Only after the astra poller reports
   118	availability on owner inbox~\#26 does the Codex route become
   119	\texttt{dispatch.sh --role mathfix} with astra.  A change to a mathematical
   120	definition or game is escalated immediately; other repairs reach the owner
   121	inbox only after the shared convergence budget expires.
   122	
   123	Sometimes an investigation uncovers an improvement that is not a discrepancy:
   124	the formalization works correctly, but it could be simplified by using an
   125	existing library, replacing a custom type, or adopting a cleaner proof route.
   126	These are not, by themselves, paper-gap notes.  They are action items.  When
   127	such an improvement is identified, open a GitHub issue or pull request that
   128	describes the proposed change.  If the investigation also produces a paper-gap
   129	note, link the issue or pull request from that note: the note records the
   130	mathematical justification, and the issue or pull request drives the
   131	implementation.
   132	
   133	\section{When to Write a Note}
   134	
   135	A note should be written once the source argument and the formal proof no longer
   136	match as mathematical arguments.  This includes, for instance, a numerical
   137	estimate whose constant does not follow from the cited lemma, a displayed
   138	conclusion which uses an unstated hypothesis, or a step in which two objects are
   139	identified although they must remain distinct.  In analytic, algebraic,
   140	probabilistic, or quantum arguments, such distinctions may concern the domain of
   141	a map, the placement of a tensor factor, the type of an outcome, the distinction
   142	between a structure and a substructure, or the scalar carried by an approximation
   143	relation.
   144	
   145	A note is required when an audit finds that a Lean declaration associated with a
   146	source-labelled statement has acquired an extra non-source hypothesis, such as
   147	bridge, residual, repair, producer, or obligation-structure data.  Such a
   148	declaration is temporary proof debt, not a replacement for the source theorem,
   149	and should not be introduced merely to avoid a \verb|sorry|.  The note must say
   150	plainly that the Lean result is conditional, identify the source-faithful theorem
   151	form that remains to be proved, and give the intended obligation discharger or
   152	removal plan.  The blueprint should not mark the source-labelled statement with
   153	\verb|\leanok| by pointing to this conditional helper.
   154	
   155	Changing a Lean theorem away from the statement in
   156	\path{references/ldt-paper/} is strongly discouraged.  A paper-gap note should
   157	not make such a change look routine: it should explain the mathematical
   158	necessity, or else classify the change as proof debt to be removed.
   159	
   160	When an existing conditional helper is audited, the first task is to extract any
   161	argument it already contains into source-faithful lemmas.  If the remaining
   162	bridge hypothesis cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the formal
   163	development should restore the source theorem statement and record the missing
   164	proof obligation explicitly, rather than retaining the strengthened statement as
   165	though it were the paper theorem.
   166	
   167	This requirement is not meant to classify every explicit Lean side condition as
   168	a discrepancy.  Positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances,
   169	and denominator nonvanishing hypotheses may be faithful encodings of the domain
   170	in which the paper's theorem is stated.  The note should distinguish such
   171	boundary hypotheses from hypotheses that supply an unproved step of the paper
   172	argument.
   173	
   174	A note is also appropriate when the proof becomes formal only after changing an
   175	intermediate scalar, weakening a conclusion, strengthening a hypothesis, or
   176	inserting an additional lemma which is not simply an expansion of the cited
   177	argument.  These are mathematical changes, even when they are harmless for the
   178	final theorem.  It is likewise appropriate when an available formal-library
   179	theorem proves the needed result under a somewhat different formulation from the
   180	cited source.  In that case the note should be deliberately pedagogical.  It
   181	should explain, in ordinary mathematical language, what the replacement result
   182	says, how it is specialized, which hypotheses are new or differently packaged,
   183	and why the resulting statement is a legitimate substitute for the step in the
   184	cited argument.  If the issue remains open after reasonable attempts, the note
   185	should say what has been checked and what remains unknown.
   186	
   187	\section{Counterexamples}
   188	
   189	If the cited assertion appears to be false, the note should not stop at saying
   190	that the proof cannot be formalized.  It should give the counterexample, or the
   191	smallest relevant part of it, in ordinary mathematical notation.  The example
   192	should be accompanied by enough verification that the reader can see both sides:
   193	the hypotheses of the cited assertion hold, and its conclusion fails.
   194	
   195	When feasible, the counterexample should also be formalized in \Lean{}.  This is
   196	especially valuable when the example is finite, algebraic, computational, or
   197	otherwise small enough that the failure can be checked without reproducing the
   198	whole surrounding theory.  The note should then state the mathematical content
   199	of the checked counterexample and identify the corresponding Lean declaration in
   200	a footnote.  The Lean file is not a substitute for the prose: the prose should
   201	still explain why the example refutes the cited assertion.
   202	
   203	\section{Revision of a Note}
   204	
   205	A paper-gap note may be provisional.  It may begin as soon as the mathematical
   206	obstruction has been isolated well enough to state the question, and it may be
   207	revised as the calculation, the blueprint, or the corresponding \Lean{}
   208	declarations become clearer.  The first version need not know the final
   209	classification, but it should say plainly which mathematical point is known and
   210	which point remains unsettled.
   211	
   212	Later revisions should not make the note into a chronological log.  They should
   213	rewrite the document so that it remains a coherent account of the present
   214	mathematical understanding.  If the verdict changes, the conclusion should state
   215	the current verdict; the linked issue or pull request can preserve the earlier
   216	discussion.
   217	
   218	\section{Form of the Note}
   219

    42	    (A : Op (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace side))) :

    48	  · congr 2

    28	/-- Simultaneous unitary conjugation preserves the quadratic form of a product. -/
    29	theorem stateQForm_conjBy_mul_apply {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]

    31	    stateQForm (applyOperatorToState U psi) (conjBy U A * conjBy U B) =
    32	      stateQForm psi (A * B) := by
    33	  rw [← stateQForm_conjTranspose_mul_mul]
    34	  congr 1
    35	  simp only [conjBy]
    36	  calc
    37	    _ = (Uᴴ * U) * A * (Uᴴ * U) * B * (Uᴴ * U) := by noncomm_ring
    38	    _ = A * B := by rw [hU]; simp

     5	
     6	Averaging the paired Pauli operators contracts the disagreement norm. The X
     7	and Z averages multiply to the EPR projection, giving the corrected projection
     8	estimate directly in the squared-distance formulation.

    10	## References

    28	/-- The averaged paired Pauli operator has squared displacement at most the
    29	mean squared disagreement between the two players. This is Jensen's inequality
    30	in the projection argument at paper lines 1715-1750. -/
    31	theorem norm_sub_pauliCorrelation_sq_le
    32	    (W : PauliKind) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (R × ((I → K) × (I → K)))) :
    33	    ‖psi - applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (1 : Op R) (pauliCorrelation W)) psi‖ ^ 2 ≤
    34	      opDistSq (uniformDistribution (I → K))
    35	        (fun u => heteroKron (1 : Op R) (heteroKron (tauObservable W u) 1))
    36	        (fun u => heteroKron (1 : Op R) (heteroKron 1 (tauObservable W u))) psi := by
    37	  classical
    38	  let L (u : I → K) :=
    39	    heteroKron (1 : Op R) (heteroKron (tauObservable W u) (1 : Op (I → K)))
    40	  let B (u : I → K) :=
    41	    heteroKron (1 : Op R) (heteroKron (1 : Op (I → K)) (tauObservable W u))
    42	  let C (u : I → K) :=
    43	    heteroKron (1 : Op R) (heteroKron (tauObservable W u) (tauObservable W u))
    44	  have hL (u : I → K) : (L u)ᴴ * L u = 1 := by
    45	    simp only [L, MagicSquareRigidity.heteroKron_conjTranspose, Matrix.conjTranspose_one,
    46	      heteroKron_mul, Matrix.one_mul, tauObservable_conjTranspose_mul_self,
    47	      heteroKron_one_one]
    48	  have halg (u : I → K) : L u * (L u - B u) = 1 - C u := by
    49	    simp only [L, B, C, Matrix.mul_sub, heteroKron_mul, Matrix.one_mul,
    50	      Matrix.mul_one, tauObservable_sq, heteroKron_one_one]
    51	  have hdist : opDistSq (uniformDistribution (I → K)) (fun _ => 1) C psi =
    52	      opDistSq (uniformDistribution (I → K)) L B psi := by
    53	    unfold opDistSq opFamilyDistSq
    54	    simp only [Fintype.sum_unique]
    55	    apply avgOver_congr
    56	    intro u
    57	    rw [← halg, MagicSquareRigidity.norm_applyOperatorToState_isometry_mul (hL u)]
    58	  have havg : averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution (I → K))
    59	      (fun u => (1 : ℂ) • ((1 : Op (R × ((I → K) × (I → K)))) - C u)) =
    60	      1 - heteroKron (1 : Op R) (pauliCorrelation W) := by
    61	    simp only [one_smul]
    62	    have hsub : averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution (I → K))
    63	        (fun u => (1 : Op (R × ((I → K) × (I → K)))) - C u) =
    64	        averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution (I → K)) (fun _ => 1) -
    65	          averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution (I → K)) C := by
    66	      simp [averageOperatorOverDistribution, smul_sub, Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    67	    rw [hsub, averageOperatorOverDistribution_const_of_isProbability _
    68	      (uniformDistribution_isProbability _)]
    69	    congr 1
    70	    rw [averageOperatorOverDistribution_uniform_eq_inv_card_smul_sum]
    71	    change _ = (Matrix.kroneckerBilinear (R := ℂ) (α := ℂ) (1 : Op R)) _
    72	    simp only [pauliCorrelation, map_smul, map_sum, C]
    73	    rfl
    74	  have h := avg_closeness (uniformDistribution (I → K))
    75	    (uniformDistribution_isProbability _) (fun _ => 1) C (fun _ => 1)
    76	    (fun _ => by simp) psi
    77	  rw [havg, hdist] at h
    78	  simpa only [MagicSquareRigidity.applyOperatorToState_sub_op,
    79	    MagicSquareRigidity.applyOperatorToState_one] using h
    80	
    81	/-- Bounds on both Pauli disagreements imply proximity to the EPR subspace.
    82	The auxiliary register is arbitrary, and the estimate requires no division
    83	by a projection norm or restriction to nonzero projection. -/
    84	theorem norm_sub_eprProjection_le_of_pauli_dist
    85	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (R × ((I → K) × (I → K))))
    86	    (delta : ℝ) (hdelta : 0 ≤ delta)
    87	    (hdist : ∀ W : PauliKind,
    88	      opDistSq (uniformDistribution (I → K))
    89	        (fun u => heteroKron (1 : Op R) (heteroKron (tauObservable W u) 1))
    90	        (fun u => heteroKron (1 : Op R) (heteroKron 1 (tauObservable W u))) psi ≤ delta) :
    91	    ‖psi - applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (1 : Op R)
    92	      (Matrix.vecMulVec (fun x => eprState (I → K) x)
    93	        (fun y => star (eprState (I → K) y)))) psi‖ ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt delta := by
    94	  let H (W : PauliKind) := heteroKron (1 : Op R) (pauliCorrelation (K := K) (ι := I) W)
    95	  have hstep (W : PauliKind) : ‖psi - applyOperatorToState (H W) psi‖ ≤ Real.sqrt delta := by
    96	    have h := (norm_sub_pauliCorrelation_sq_le W psi).trans (hdist W)
    97	    exact (Real.le_sqrt (norm_nonneg _) hdelta).mpr h
    98	  have hprod : H .X * H .Z = heteroKron (1 : Op R)
    99	      (Matrix.vecMulVec (fun x => eprState (I → K) x)
   100	        (fun y => star (eprState (I → K) y))) := by
   101	    dsimp only [H]
   102	    rw [heteroKron_mul, Matrix.one_mul, pauliCorrelation_mul_eq_epr]
   103	  rw [← hprod, applyOperatorToState_mul]
   104	  calc
   105	    _ ≤ ‖psi - applyOperatorToState (H .X) psi‖ +
   106	        ‖applyOperatorToState (H .X) psi -
   107	          applyOperatorToState (H .X) (applyOperatorToState (H .Z) psi)‖ :=
   108	      norm_sub_le_norm_sub_add_norm_sub _ _ _
   109	    _ ≤ Real.sqrt delta + Real.sqrt delta := add_le_add (hstep .X) (by
   110	      rw [← MagicSquareRigidity.applyOperatorToState_sub]
   111	      exact (norm_heteroKron_pauliCorrelation_apply_le .X _).trans (hstep .Z))
   112	    _ = 2 * Real.sqrt delta := by ring
   113	
   114	end

     4	/-!

     6	
     7	The product of the averaged, paired X and Z observables is the rank-one
     8	projection onto the EPR vector. This is an algebraic prerequisite for constructing
     9	the auxiliary state in `exists_extractionWitness_ofGlobalPairWitness`.

    11	## References
    12	
    13	Blueprint `lem:qld-unitary`; paper

    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT.Extraction

    25	variable {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
    26	  [Algebra (ZMod 2) K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    27	
    28	/-- The operator `H_W` of the EPR projection argument, averaged over all
    29	generalized Pauli labels. Paper lines 1725-1733 define this average after
    30	reindexing by a nonzero element of the binary basis. -/
    31	def pauliCorrelation (W : PauliKind) : Op ((ι → K) × (ι → K)) :=
    32	  (Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ)⁻¹ •
    33	    ∑ u : ι → K, heteroKron (tauObservable W u) (tauObservable W u)
    34	
    35	private theorem avg_phaseSign_dotProduct (v : ι → K) :
    36	    (Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ)⁻¹ *
    37	        ∑ u : ι → K, phaseSign (binTrace K (dotProduct u v)) =
    38	      if v = 0 then 1 else 0 := by
    39	  have h := congrArg (fun A : Op (ι → K) => A v v)
    40	    (pauliProj_eq_avg_tauObservable .Z (0 : ι → K))
    41	  have hv : pauliProj .Z (0 : ι → K) v v = if v = 0 then 1 else 0 := by
    42	    change (∏ i, if v i = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0) *
    43	      star (∏ i, if v i = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0) = _
    44	    simp only [Fintype.prod_boole, ← funext_iff]
    45	    change (if v = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0) * star (if v = 0 then 1 else 0) = _
    46	    split <;> simp
    47	  simp only [dotProduct_zero, map_zero, phaseSign, ite_true, one_smul] at h
    48	  rw [hv] at h
    49	  simpa only [Matrix.smul_apply, Matrix.sum_apply, smul_eq_mul,
    50	    tauObservable_Z_apply, ite_true, one_mul] using h.symm

    52	      (inner ℂ (psi - phi) (applyOperatorToState T psi)).re +
    53	        (inner ℂ phi (applyOperatorToState T (psi - phi))).re := by
    54	    simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState]
    55	  rw [hsplit]
    56	  calc
    57	    _ ≤ |(inner ℂ (psi - phi) (applyOperatorToState T psi)).re| +
    58	        |(inner ℂ phi (applyOperatorToState T (psi - phi))).re| := abs_add_le _ _
    59	    _ ≤ ‖psi - phi‖ * ‖applyOperatorToState T psi‖ +
    60	        ‖phi‖ * ‖applyOperatorToState T (psi - phi)‖ :=
    61	      add_le_add ((Complex.abs_re_le_norm _).trans (norm_inner_le_norm _ _))
    62	        ((Complex.abs_re_le_norm _).trans (norm_inner_le_norm _ _))
    63	    _ ≤ ‖psi - phi‖ * ‖psi‖ + ‖phi‖ * ‖psi - phi‖ :=
    64	      add_le_add (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hT psi) (norm_nonneg _))
    65	        (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hT (psi - phi)) (norm_nonneg _))
    66	    _ = _ := by rw [hpsi, hphi]; ring

    68	/-- The complete diagonal overlap of two local measurements is stable under a
    69	change of unit state. The tensor factors can have different dimensions. -/
    70	theorem abs_diagonal_overlap_state_sub_le {α I J : Type*}
    71	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    72	    [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J] (A : Measurement α I) (B : Measurement α J)
    73	    (psi phi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J)) (hpsi : ‖psi‖ = 1) (hphi : ‖phi‖ = 1) :
    74	    |(∑ a, stateQForm psi (heteroKron (A.effect a) (B.effect a))) -
    75	      ∑ a, stateQForm phi (heteroKron (A.effect a) (B.effect a))| ≤
    76	        2 * ‖psi - phi‖ := by
    77	  let s := Finset.univ.filter (fun ab : α × α => ab.1 = ab.2)
    78	  have heq : (∑ ab ∈ s, (tensorMeasurement A B).effect ab) =
    79	      ∑ a, heteroKron (A.effect a) (B.effect a) := by
    80	    simp [s, Finset.sum_filter, Fintype.sum_prod_type, tensorMeasurement,
    81	      Measurement.ofSumEqOne]
    82	  have h := abs_stateQForm_sub_le_of_contraction _
    83	    (norm_apply_measurement_sum_le (tensorMeasurement A B) s) psi phi hpsi hphi
    84	  rw [heq, stateQForm_finset_sum, stateQForm_finset_sum] at h
    85	  exact h

    87	/-- Averaging evaluated overlaps does not increase the state-transfer cost.
    88	This controls the complete overlap in paper `eq:qld-unitary-9`. -/
    89	theorem evaluated_overlap_state_transfer {Y α R I J : Type*}
    90	    [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y] [Nonempty Y]
    91	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R]
    92	    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
    93	    (A : Measurement α I) (B : Measurement α J) (eval : α → Y → R)
    94	    (psi phi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J)) (hpsi : ‖psi‖ = 1) (hphi : ‖phi‖ = 1) :
    95	    avgOver (uniformDistribution Y) (fun y => ∑ r, stateQForm psi
    96	      (heteroKron ((A.postprocess (fun a => eval a y)).effect r)
    97	        ((B.postprocess (fun a => eval a y)).effect r))) ≤
    98	      avgOver (uniformDistribution Y) (fun y => ∑ r, stateQForm phi
    99	        (heteroKron ((A.postprocess (fun a => eval a y)).effect r)
   100	          ((B.postprocess (fun a => eval a y)).effect r))) + 2 * ‖psi - phi‖ := by
   101	  have h := avgOver_mono (uniformDistribution Y) _ _ (fun y =>
   102	    (le_abs_self _).trans (abs_diagonal_overlap_state_sub_le
   103	      (A.postprocess (fun a => eval a y)) (B.postprocess (fun a => eval a y))
   104	      psi phi hpsi hphi))
   105	  rw [avgOver_sub, avgOver_const_of_isProbability _
   106	    (uniformDistribution_isProbability _)] at h
   107	  linarith

   109	/-- Two distinct Pauli answers have encodings agreeing on at most an `md/q`
   110	fraction of points. Injectivity follows from the exact decoder identity. -/
   111	theorem pauli_encoding_collision_le {P : AdmissibleParams}
   112	    (h k : PauliRegister P) (hne : h ≠ k) :
   113	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
   114	      (fun u => if evalPoly (encodingPoly h) u = evalPoly (encodingPoly k) u
   115	        then (1 : ℝ) else 0) ≤ (P.m * P.d : ℝ) / P.q := by
   116	  apply poly_eval_collision_le
   117	  intro heq
   118	  apply hne
   119	  have hd := congrArg (fun g : Poly P => decodeFq g) heq
   120	  simpa only [decodeFq_lowDegreeEncoding] using hd
   121	
   122	/-- The unevaluated Pauli overlap on a unit comparison state is bounded below
   123	by the evaluated overlap on another unit state, minus the collision and state
   124	errors. This combines paper `eq:qld-unitary-8` with the transfer following
   125	`eq:qld-unitary-9`, without any dimension or answer-count factor. -/
   126	theorem pauli_overlap_transfer {P : AdmissibleParams} {I J : Type*}
   127	    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   128	    (A : Measurement (PauliRegister P) I) (B : Measurement (PauliRegister P) J)
   129	    (theta ideal : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J))
   130	    (htheta : ‖theta‖ = 1) (hideal : ‖ideal‖ = 1) :
   131	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) (fun u =>
   132	      ∑ a : PauliScalar P, stateQForm theta
   133	        (heteroKron ((A.postprocess (fun h => evalPoly (encodingPoly h) u)).effect a)
   134	          ((B.postprocess (fun h => evalPoly (encodingPoly h) u)).effect a))) ≤
   135	      (∑ h, stateQForm ideal (heteroKron (A.effect h) (B.effect h))) +
   136	        (P.m * P.d : ℝ) / P.q + 2 * ‖theta - ideal‖ := by
   137	  have ht := evaluated_overlap_state_transfer A B
   138	    (fun h u => evalPoly (encodingPoly h) u) theta ideal htheta hideal
   139	  have hc := SandwichProduct.avg_diagonal_postprocess_stateQForm_le A B ideal
   140	    (fun h u => evalPoly (encodingPoly h) u) ((P.m * P.d : ℝ) / P.q) hideal
   141	    (by positivity) pauli_encoding_collision_le
   142	  exact ht.trans (add_le_add hc le_rfl)
   143	
   144	end

    29	/-- A symmetric operator acts identically on the two halves of the extracted

    33	    [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty V]
    34	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J)) (T : Op V) (hT : Tᵀ = T) :
    35	    applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (heteroKron (1 : Op I) T) (1 : Op (J × V)))
    36	        (reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor aux (eprState V))) =
    37	      applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (1 : Op (I × V)) (heteroKron (1 : Op J) T))
    38	        (reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor aux (eprState V))) := by
    39	  ext p

    44	  rw [show T p.2.2 p.1.2 = T p.1.2 p.2.2 from congrFun (congrFun hT p.1.2) p.2.2]

    47	/-- The full answer-summed Pauli distance on `aux tensor EPR` is at most twice
    48	the evaluated-overlap deficit on `theta`, plus `2md/q` and four times the state
    49	distance. The bound holds for every local POVM and every normalized auxiliary
    50	state, with no restriction on the field, Pauli basis, or local dimensions.
    51	This is the quantitative combination of paper `eq:qld-unitary-7` through
    52	`eq:qld-unitary-9` and its following state-transfer estimate. -/
    53	theorem pauli_distance_on_ideal_le {P : AdmissibleParams} {I J : Type*}
    54	    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
    55	    (A : Measurement (PauliRegister P) (I × PauliRegister P)) (W : PauliKind)
    56	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J)) (haux : ‖aux‖ = 1)
    57	    (theta : EuclideanSpace ℂ ((I × PauliRegister P) × (J × PauliRegister P)))
    58	    (htheta : ‖theta‖ = 1) :
    59	    let ideal := reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor aux (eprState (PauliRegister P)))
    60	    let B := rightPlacedMeasurement (ιA := J) (pauliRegisterMeas (params := P) W)
    61	    (∑ h : PauliRegister P, ‖applyOperatorToState
    62	      (heteroKron (A.effect h - heteroKron (1 : Op I) (pauliProj W h))
    63	        (1 : Op (J × PauliRegister P))) ideal‖ ^ 2) ≤
    64	      2 * (1 - avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) (fun u =>
    65	        ∑ a : PauliScalar P, stateQForm theta
    66	          (heteroKron ((A.postprocess (fun h => evalPoly (encodingPoly h) u)).effect a)
    67	            ((B.postprocess (fun h => evalPoly (encodingPoly h) u)).effect a)))) +
    68	        2 * ((P.m * P.d : ℝ) / P.q) + 4 * ‖theta - ideal‖ := by
    69	  dsimp only
    70	  let ideal := reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor aux (eprState (PauliRegister P)))
    71	  let B := rightPlacedMeasurement (ιA := J) (pauliRegisterMeas (params := P) W)
    72	  have hideal : ‖ideal‖ = 1 := by
    73	    rw [reindexState_norm_eq, vecTensor_norm_eq, haux, eprState_norm, one_mul]
    74	  have hdist := point_distance_le_two_defect
    75	    (leftPlacedMeasurement (ιB := J × PauliRegister P) A)
    76	    (rightPlacedMeasurement (ιA := I × PauliRegister P) B) ideal
    77	  rw [point_defect_eq, hideal, one_pow] at hdist
    78	  have haction (h : PauliRegister P) :
    79	      applyOperatorToState
    80	          (heteroKron (A.effect h - heteroKron (1 : Op I) (pauliProj W h))
    81	            (1 : Op (J × PauliRegister P))) ideal =
    82	        applyOperatorToState
    83	          ((leftPlacedMeasurement (ιB := J × PauliRegister P) A).effect h -
    84	            (rightPlacedMeasurement (ιA := I × PauliRegister P) B).effect h) ideal := by
    85	    change applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (A.effect h - _) _) ideal =
    86	      applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (A.effect h) _ -
    87	        heteroKron _ (heteroKron _ (pauliProj W h))) ideal
    88	    rw [heteroKron_sub_left, MagicSquareRigidity.applyOperatorToState_sub_op,
    89	      MagicSquareRigidity.applyOperatorToState_sub_op,
    90	      extracted_epr_actions_eq aux _ (pauliProj_transpose W h)]
    91	  have hsum := Finset.sum_congr (s₁ := (Finset.univ : Finset (PauliRegister P)))
    92	    rfl (fun h _ => congrArg (fun v => ‖v‖ ^ 2) (haction h))
    93	  rw [hsum]
    94	  have hoverlap := pauli_overlap_transfer A B theta ideal htheta hideal
    95	  simp only [leftPlacedMeasurement, rightPlacedMeasurement, Measurement.ofSumEqOne,
    96	    placed_product_stateQForm_eq] at hdist
    97	  exact hdist.trans (by dsimp [B] at hoverlap ⊢; linarith)

    99	/-- At construction error at most one, a universal extraction coefficient of
   100	at least eighteen absorbs both the proved state error and the Pauli comparison
   101	error. The collision term and fourth-root scale are exactly those of
   102	`deltaExtract`; there is no parameter-dependent enlargement of the constant. -/
   103	theorem extraction_small_error_absorption (C delta : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ)
   104	    (hC : 18 ≤ C) (hdelta : 0 ≤ delta) (hdelta_one : delta ≤ 1) :
   105	    16 * delta ≤ deltaExtract C delta m d q ∧
   106	      2 * delta + 2 * (((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / q) + 16 * Real.sqrt delta ≤
   107	        deltaExtract C delta m d q := by
   108	  have hroot := Real.self_le_rpow_of_le_one hdelta hdelta_one
   109	    (by norm_num : (1 / 4 : ℝ) ≤ 1)
   110	  have hsqrt : Real.sqrt delta ≤ delta ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) := by
   111	    rw [Real.sqrt_eq_rpow]
   112	    exact Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_ge' hdelta hdelta_one (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   113	  have hr : 0 ≤ (((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / q) := by positivity
   114	  have hp := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hC
   115	    (add_nonneg (Real.rpow_nonneg hdelta (1 / 4)) hr)
   116	  constructor
   117	  · exact (show 16 * delta ≤ 18 * (delta ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) +
   118	      ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / q) by nlinarith).trans hp
   119	  · exact (show 2 * delta + 2 * (((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / q) + 16 * Real.sqrt delta ≤
   120	      18 * (delta ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) + ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / q) by nlinarith).trans hp
   121	
   122	end

 \section{Numerical defects in the source proof}
 
 Lines~1715--1742 of
 \path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}
 construct $H_X,H_Z$ and identify $H_XH_Z$ with the EPR projection.  The norm
 estimate at lines~1743--1750 gives
 $\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert\leq\sqrt\delta$.  At lines~1753--1757 the
 source substitutes $\delta$ inside the reverse triangle inequality
 \cite[lines~1715--1783]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  That replacement is not valid for
 small $\delta$.  The desired lower bound on
 $\langle H_W^2\rangle$ follows directly from $H_W^2\geq2H_W-I$, as above.
 
 The triangle inequality yields
 \[
   \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert\leq2\sqrt\delta,
 \]

 \section{The range-projection obligation}
 
 Lines~1827--1858 prove state-dependent closeness for the concrete operators
 obtained by conjugating the original measurement with the swap unitaries.
 Lines~1864--1875 then define isometries by adjoining EPR pairs and applying
 those unitaries, and immediately state the corresponding closeness for
 $\phi M_h\phi^\dagger$.  The omitted range projection makes this implication
 non-definitional \cite[lines~1827--1875]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
 
 Let $\Psi$ be the original state and suppose $\phi\Psi$ is close to the ideal
 state $\Delta$.  Since $Q\phi\Psi=\phi\Psi$ and $Q$ is a contraction, the
 triangle inequality bounds $(I-Q)\Delta$ by the state-extraction error.  Using
 $\phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ$, split
 \[
   (N_hQ-T_h)\Delta
   =(N_h-T_h)\Delta-N_h(I-Q)\Delta,
 \]

 uses projectivity and orthogonality to keep the second term under control.
 The same argument is required for each player and each Pauli basis.

    34	      opDistSq (uniformDistribution (I → K))
    35	        (fun u => heteroKron (1 : Op R) (heteroKron (tauObservable W u) 1))
    36	        (fun u => heteroKron (1 : Op R) (heteroKron 1 (tauObservable W u))) psi := by

    39	    heteroKron (1 : Op R) (heteroKron (tauObservable W u) (1 : Op (I → K)))
    40	  let B (u : I → K) :=
    41	    heteroKron (1 : Op R) (heteroKron (1 : Op (I → K)) (tauObservable W u))
    42	  let C (u : I → K) :=
    43	    heteroKron (1 : Op R) (heteroKron (tauObservable W u) (tauObservable W u))

    87	    (hdist : ∀ W : PauliKind,

   107	          applyOperatorToState (H .X) (applyOperatorToState (H .Z) psi)‖ :=

    92	    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]

   103	      (A.postprocess (fun a => eval a y)) (B.postprocess (fun a => eval a y))
   104	      psi phi hpsi hphi))

   106	    (uniformDistribution_isProbability _)] at h

   116	  apply poly_eval_collision_le

   138	    (fun h u => evalPoly (encodingPoly h) u) theta ideal htheta hideal
   139	  have hc := SandwichProduct.avg_diagonal_postprocess_stateQForm_le A B ideal
   140	    (fun h u => evalPoly (encodingPoly h) u) ((P.m * P.d : ℝ) / P.q) hideal

    34	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J)) (T : Op V) (hT : Tᵀ = T) :

    54	    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
    55	    (A : Measurement (PauliRegister P) (I × PauliRegister P)) (W : PauliKind)
    56	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J)) (haux : ‖aux‖ = 1)
    57	    (theta : EuclideanSpace ℂ ((I × PauliRegister P) × (J × PauliRegister P)))
    58	    (htheta : ‖theta‖ = 1) :
    59	    let ideal := reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor aux (eprState (PauliRegister P)))
    60	    let B := rightPlacedMeasurement (ιA := J) (pauliRegisterMeas (params := P) W)
    61	    (∑ h : PauliRegister P, ‖applyOperatorToState
    62	      (heteroKron (A.effect h - heteroKron (1 : Op I) (pauliProj W h))
    63	        (1 : Op (J × PauliRegister P))) ideal‖ ^ 2) ≤
    64	      2 * (1 - avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) (fun u =>
    65	        ∑ a : PauliScalar P, stateQForm theta
    66	          (heteroKron ((A.postprocess (fun h => evalPoly (encodingPoly h) u)).effect a)
    67	            ((B.postprocess (fun h => evalPoly (encodingPoly h) u)).effect a)))) +
    68	        2 * ((P.m * P.d : ℝ) / P.q) + 4 * ‖theta - ideal‖ := by
    69	  dsimp only
    70	  let ideal := reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor aux (eprState (PauliRegister P)))
    71	  let B := rightPlacedMeasurement (ιA := J) (pauliRegisterMeas (params := P) W)
    72	  have hideal : ‖ideal‖ = 1 := by
    73	    rw [reindexState_norm_eq, vecTensor_norm_eq, haux, eprState_norm, one_mul]
    74	  have hdist := point_distance_le_two_defect
    75	    (leftPlacedMeasurement (ιB := J × PauliRegister P) A)
    76	    (rightPlacedMeasurement (ιA := I × PauliRegister P) B) ideal
    77	  rw [point_defect_eq, hideal, one_pow] at hdist
    78	  have haction (h : PauliRegister P) :
    79	      applyOperatorToState

    81	            (1 : Op (J × PauliRegister P))) ideal =
    82	        applyOperatorToState
    83	          ((leftPlacedMeasurement (ιB := J × PauliRegister P) A).effect h -
    84	            (rightPlacedMeasurement (ιA := I × PauliRegister P) B).effect h) ideal := by

    95	  simp only [leftPlacedMeasurement, rightPlacedMeasurement, Measurement.ofSumEqOne,
    96	    placed_product_stateQForm_eq] at hdist
    97	  exact hdist.trans (by dsimp [B] at hoverlap ⊢; linarith)

    99	/-- At construction error at most one, a universal extraction coefficient of
   100	at least eighteen absorbs both the proved state error and the Pauli comparison
   101	error. The collision term and fourth-root scale are exactly those of
   102	`deltaExtract`; there is no parameter-dependent enlargement of the constant. -/
   103	theorem extraction_small_error_absorption (C delta : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ)
   104	    (hC : 18 ≤ C) (hdelta : 0 ≤ delta) (hdelta_one : delta ≤ 1) :
   105	    16 * delta ≤ deltaExtract C delta m d q ∧
   106	      2 * delta + 2 * (((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / q) + 16 * Real.sqrt delta ≤
   107	        deltaExtract C delta m d q := by
   108	  have hroot := Real.self_le_rpow_of_le_one hdelta hdelta_one
   109	    (by norm_num : (1 / 4 : ℝ) ≤ 1)
   110	  have hsqrt : Real.sqrt delta ≤ delta ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) := by
   111	    rw [Real.sqrt_eq_rpow]
   112	    exact Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_ge' hdelta hdelta_one (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   113	  have hr : 0 ≤ (((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / q) := by positivity
   114	  have hp := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hC
   115	    (add_nonneg (Real.rpow_nonneg hdelta (1 / 4)) hr)
   116	  constructor
   117	  · exact (show 16 * delta ≤ 18 * (delta ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) +
   118	      ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / q) by nlinarith).trans hp
   119	  · exact (show 2 * delta + 2 * (((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / q) + 16 * Real.sqrt delta ≤
   120	      18 * (delta ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) + ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / q) by nlinarith).trans hp
   121

   234	/-- The composed construction and extraction errors preserve the error family
   235	of `thm:pauli`: when `deltaG` has the form
   236	`deltaQld a b epsilon m d q`, the result is bounded by another member of that
   237	family after decreasing the exponent and enlarging the universal constant.
   238	
   239	This is `lem:qld-extraction-error-form` in the blueprint and the named
   240	quantitative obligation behind `rem:pauli-robustness-form`; the concluding
   241	paper comparison is at
   242	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1855-1858,1868-1876`.
   243	
   244	One may take `a' = 4 * C^2 * a` and `b' = b / 8`. Subadditivity of the
   245	fourth root bounds the three construction terms separately. Admissibility
   246	gives `md ≥ 1` and `q ≥ 1`, so their polynomial factors and the term `md/q`
   247	are absorbed into the enlarged prefactor. This discharges the scalar
   248	estimate tracked by issue #241. -/
   249	theorem deltaExtract_le_deltaQld (C a b : ℝ) (hC : 1 ≤ C) (ha : 1 < a)
   250	    (hb : 0 < b) (hb1 : b < 1) :
   251	    ∃ a' b' : ℝ, 1 ≤ a' ∧ 0 < b' ∧ b' < 1 ∧
   252	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (epsilon : ℝ), 0 ≤ epsilon →
   253	        epsilon ≤ 1 →
   254	        deltaExtract C
   255	            (deltaConstructPaulis C epsilon
   256	              (deltaQld a b epsilon P.m P.d P.q) P.m P.d P.q)
   257	            P.m P.d P.q ≤
   258	          deltaQld a' b' epsilon P.m P.d P.q := by
   259	  have hC0 : 0 ≤ C := by linarith
   260	  have ha0 : 0 ≤ a := by linarith
   261	  have hconstant : a ≤ 4 * C ^ 2 * a := by
   262	    have hCsq : 1 ≤ C ^ 2 := by nlinarith
   263	    nlinarith [mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hCsq ha0]
   264	  refine ⟨4 * C ^ 2 * a, b / 8, ha.le.trans hconstant, by positivity, by linarith, ?_⟩
   265	  intro params epsilon hepsilon0 hepsilon1
   266	  let degree : ℝ := ((params.m * params.d : ℕ) : ℝ)
   267	  have hdegree1 : 1 ≤ degree :=
   268	    Nat.one_le_cast.mpr (Nat.mul_pos params.one_le_m params.hd)
   269	  have hdegree0 : 0 ≤ degree := by linarith
   270	  have hfield1 : (1 : ℝ) ≤ (params.q : ℝ) := by
   271	    obtain ⟨size, -, hsize⟩ := params.hq
   272	    rw [hsize]
   273	    exact_mod_cast Nat.one_le_pow _ _ (by norm_num)
   274	  have hfield0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (params.q : ℝ) := by positivity
   275	  let amplitude : ℝ := a * degree ^ a
   276	  let rate : ℝ := epsilon ^ (b / 8) + (params.q : ℝ) ^ (-(b / 8)) +
   277	    (2 : ℝ) ^ (-((b / 8) * degree))
   278	  have hamplitude1 : 1 ≤ amplitude :=
   279	    one_le_mul_of_one_le_of_one_le ha.le (Real.one_le_rpow hdegree1 ha0)
   280	  have hamplitude0 : 0 ≤ amplitude := by linarith
   281	  have hdegree_amplitude : degree ≤ amplitude :=
   282	    (Real.self_le_rpow_of_one_le hdegree1 ha.le).trans
   283	      (le_mul_of_one_le_left (Real.rpow_nonneg hdegree0 a) ha.le)
   284	  have hrate0 : 0 ≤ rate := by dsimp [rate]; positivity
   285	  have hepsilon_rate : epsilon ^ (b / 8) ≤ rate := by
   286	    dsimp [rate]
   287	    linarith [Real.rpow_nonneg hfield0 (-(b / 8)),
   288	      Real.rpow_nonneg (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2) (-((b / 8) * degree))]
   289	  have hfield_rate : (params.q : ℝ) ^ (-(b / 8)) ≤ rate := by
   290	    dsimp [rate]
   291	    linarith [Real.rpow_nonneg hepsilon0 (b / 8),
   292	      Real.rpow_nonneg (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2) (-((b / 8) * degree))]
   293	  have hroot_sum {first second third : ℝ}
   294	      (hfirst : 0 ≤ first) (hsecond : 0 ≤ second) (hthird : 0 ≤ third) :
   295	      (first + second + third) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) ≤
   296	        first ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) + second ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) + third ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) :=
   297	    (Real.rpow_add_le_add_rpow (p := (1 / 4 : ℝ)) (add_nonneg hfirst hsecond) hthird
   298	      (by norm_num) (by norm_num)).trans
   299	      (add_le_add (Real.rpow_add_le_add_rpow (p := (1 / 4 : ℝ)) hfirst hsecond
   300	        (by norm_num) (by norm_num)) le_rfl)
   301	  have hrate_root :
   302	      (epsilon ^ b + (params.q : ℝ) ^ (-b) + (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(b * degree))) ^
   303	        (1 / 4 : ℝ) ≤ rate := by
   304	    refine (hroot_sum (by positivity) (by positivity) (by positivity)).trans ?_
   305	    rw [← Real.rpow_mul hepsilon0, ← Real.rpow_mul hfield0,
   306	      ← Real.rpow_mul (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2)]
   307	    refine add_le_add (add_le_add ?_ ?_) ?_
   308	    · exact Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_ge' hepsilon0 hepsilon1
   309	        (by positivity) (by linarith)
   310	    · exact Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le hfield1 (by linarith)
   311	    · apply Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le (by norm_num)
   312	      nlinarith [mul_nonneg hb.le hdegree0]
   313	  have hglobal0 : 0 ≤ deltaQld a b epsilon params.m params.d params.q := by
   314	    simp only [deltaQld, Real.rpow_eq_pow]
   315	    positivity
   316	  have hglobal_root :
   317	      (deltaQld a b epsilon params.m params.d params.q) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) ≤
   318	        amplitude * rate := by
   319	    change (amplitude *
   320	      (epsilon ^ b + (params.q : ℝ) ^ (-b) + (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(b * degree)))) ^
   321	        (1 / 4 : ℝ) ≤ amplitude * rate
   322	    rw [Real.mul_rpow hamplitude0 (by positivity)]
   323	    exact mul_le_mul (Real.rpow_le_self_of_one_le hamplitude1 (by norm_num))
   324	      hrate_root (by positivity) hamplitude0
   325	  have hsqrt_root : (Real.sqrt epsilon) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) ≤ amplitude * rate := by
   326	    rw [Real.sqrt_eq_rpow, ← Real.rpow_mul hepsilon0]
   327	    exact ((Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_ge' hepsilon0 hepsilon1
   328	      (by positivity) (by linarith)).trans hepsilon_rate).trans
   329	      (le_mul_of_one_le_left hrate0 hamplitude1)
   330	  have hratio_root : (degree / (params.q : ℝ)) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) ≤ amplitude * rate := by

    28	/-- Simultaneous unitary conjugation preserves the quadratic form of a product. -/
    29	theorem stateQForm_conjBy_mul_apply {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    30	    (U A B : Op I) (hU : Uᴴ * U = 1) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ I) :
    31	    stateQForm (applyOperatorToState U psi) (conjBy U A * conjBy U B) =
    32	      stateQForm psi (A * B) := by
    33	  rw [← stateQForm_conjTranspose_mul_mul]
    34	  congr 1
    35	  simp only [conjBy]
    36	  calc
    37	    _ = (Uᴴ * U) * A * (Uᴴ * U) * B * (Uᴴ * U) := by noncomm_ring
    38	    _ = A * B := by rw [hU]; simp

    45	/-- The total Pauli POVM extended to the full local extraction block and
    46	conjugated by the concrete swap. This is the measurement in `eq:qld-unitary-7`. -/
    47	def swappedPauliMeas (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG) (side : PlayerSide)
    48	    (W : PauliKind) : Measurement (PauliRegister P) (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace side)) :=
    49	  Measurement.ofSumEqOne
    50	    (fun h => conjBy (swapUnitary w side) (S.onPlayer side ((S.pauliMeas side W).effect h)))
    51	    (fun h => by
    52	      apply star_right_conjugate_nonneg
    53	      exact kronecker_nonneg
    54	        (kronecker_nonneg ((S.pauliMeas side W).pos h) Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg)
    55	        Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg)
    56	    (by
    57	      simp only [conjBy, onPlayer, ← Finset.sum_mul, ← Matrix.mul_sum,
    58	        ← heteroKron_finset_sum_left, (S.pauliMeas side W).sum_eq_one,
    59	        heteroKron_one_one, Matrix.mul_one, swapUnitary_mul_conjTranspose])

   156	/-- On the jointly swapped state, the overlap of conjugated block measurements
   157	is one minus their original consistency defect. This is simultaneous unitary
   158	invariance with the exact six-register reassociation. -/
   159	theorem swapped_block_overlap_eq (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG)
   160	    {X α : Type*} [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   161	    (mu : Distribution X) (hmu : mu.IsProbability)
   162	    (A : X → Measurement α (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιA))
   163	    (B : X → Measurement α (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιB)) :
   164	    avgOver mu (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm
   165	      (reindexState (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
   166	        (S.applyBoth (swapUnitary w .alice) (swapUnitary w .bob) S.psiHat))
   167	      (heteroKron (conjBy (swapUnitary w .alice) ((A x).effect a))
   168	        (conjBy (swapUnitary w .bob) ((B x).effect a)))) =
   169	      1 - consistencyDefect mu
   170	        (fun x a => S.placeSide .alice ((A x).effect a))
   171	        (fun x a => S.placeSide .bob ((B x).effect a)) S.psiHat := by
   172	  have h := consistencyDefect_eq_one_sub_overlap mu
   173	    (fun x => S.blockMeasurement .alice (A x))

   175	  simp only [blockMeasurement_effect] at h

  1415	 \subsection{Pulling the $X$ and $Z$ measurements apart}

  1418	
  1419	Recall the decoding map of the low-degree code defined in \Cref{sec:ld-encoding}. This map takes in a polynomial $g \in \ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$ and returns a string $\coded(g) \in \F_q^{\nqubits}$ consisting of the evaluations of $g$ on the points in the hypercube $\{0,1\}^m$.
  1420	We now use this decoding map to construct a new set of measurement operators out of $\hat{S}$.
  1421	First, we introduce some notation. For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and all degree $d$ polynomials $g: \F_q^m \to \F_q$ define projectors
  1422	\[ \hat{S}^X_g = \sum_{g_\zpt} \hat{S}_{g,g_\zpt} \quad  \text{and}  \quad \hat{S}^Z_g = \sum_{g_\xpt} \hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g}\;,\]
  1423	where the measurement $\{\hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \}$  is given by \Cref{lem:qld-4-7}.
  1424	
  1425	For all $W \in \{X, Z\}$, $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^{\nqubits}$, and $a \in \F_q$, define the projector
  1426	\begin{equation}\label{eq:def-tauwu}
  1427	 \tau^{W}_{a}(\tilde{u}) = \sum_{h \in \F_q^{\nqubits} \,:\, h \cdot \tilde{u} = a} \tau^W_{h}
  1428	\end{equation}
  1429	where recall that $\tau^W_h$ is the projector corresponding to measuring $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$ in the $W$ basis and obtaining $h \in \F_q^\nqubits$ as the outcome. For all $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits$ define the projective measurement $\{ \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \}_{a \in \F_q}$ by 
  1430		\begin{equation}
  1431		\label{eq:tilde_M}
  1432		\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a =  \sum_{g} \hat{S}^W_g \otimes \tau_{(\coded(g) \cdot \tilde{u}) - a}^W(\tilde{u})\;.
  1433		\end{equation}
  1434		If $\hat{S}^W_g$ is viewed as an operator acting on registers $\alice \alice'$ (resp. $\bob \bob'$) then we view $\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a$ as an operator acting on registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ (resp. $\bob \bob' \bob''$). (When necessary we will indicate via subscripts which registers the operators are acting on.)
  1435	The $\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a$ are projective because the $\hat{S}^W_g$ and $\tau^W$ operators are projective.
  1436	
  1437
